source: Vaccaro, Almaatouq, Malone (2024) When are combinations of humans and AI useful? Meta-analysis
finding: Across studies, human-AI teams did worse than the best of human alone or AI alone.
numbers: Pre-registered. 74 papers, 106 experiments, 370 effect sizes (Jan 2020-Jun 2023). Synergy g=-0.23 (95% CI -0.39 to -0.07, p=.005). Versus human alone: g=0.64 (CI 0.53-0.74).
limits: Only lab-style studies chosen by researchers; about 85% of effect sizes are decision tasks; heterogeneity I2=97.7%.
agent_relevance: A tool-plus-model system is not automatically better than the better part. We must test the joint system against the stronger part alone, per task.

source: Vaccaro, Almaatouq, Malone (2024) When are combinations of humans and AI useful? Meta-analysis
finding: Task type moderates synergy: decision tasks lose, content-creation tasks gain.
numbers: Decision tasks g=-0.27 (CI -0.44 to -0.10). Creation tasks g=0.19 (CI -0.09 to 0.48, n=34 effect sizes, not significant alone). Difference between types p=.006.
limits: Creation estimate is imprecise. Authors say creation tasks hold routine generation that AI does well.
agent_relevance: Let the model draft and generate; do not make a weak final pick the deciding step. Fits the split of program and model roles.

source: Vaccaro, Almaatouq, Malone (2024) When are combinations of humans and AI useful? Meta-analysis
finding: Relative skill decides who should hold the final say.
numbers: When human alone beat AI alone: synergy g=0.46 (CI 0.28-0.66). When AI alone beat human: g=-0.54 (CI -0.71 to -0.37). Augmentation over human when AI was better: g=0.74.
limits: Over 95% of systems had the human make the final decision; so the finding is about human-final designs, not all allocations.
agent_relevance: Whoever is weaker at a sub-step should not own the decision on it. Route final authority by measured skill, not by habit.

source: Vaccaro, Almaatouq, Malone (2024) When are combinations of humans and AI useful? Meta-analysis
finding: Explanations and confidence displays did not significantly change synergy.
numbers: Moderators explanation, confidence, participant type, division of labor all not significant for synergy or augmentation.
limits: Heterogeneity mostly unexplained; interactions not modelled.
agent_relevance: Adding rationale text or a confidence number to a handoff is not a proven fix by itself.

source: Bansal et al. (2021) Does the whole exceed its parts? Effect of AI explanations on complementary team performance
finding: With AI accuracy matched to human accuracy, teams beat both alone, but explanations added nothing over a confidence score.
numbers: MTurk, about 100 per condition. Beer reviews: human 0.82, AI 0.84, team with confidence 0.89 vs team with Explain-Top-1 0.88 (t=-1.18, p=.24). LSAT (20 items): AI 65%, human 67%, confidence team gain +20.1% relative. Amzbook gain only +2.2%.
limits: Crowd workers, small tasks; Amzbook had human and AI errors strongly correlated, so little room. Bonus design may shape strategy.
agent_relevance: Complementarity needs low error overlap between partners. Check overlap of program checks and model errors.

source: Bansal et al. (2021)
finding: Explanations raised acceptance of AI advice even when the AI was wrong.
numbers: Explain-Top-1 worsened accuracy on AI-wrong items for Beer and LSAT; Explain-Top-1 vs Explain-Top-2 not different (Beer p=.40, Amzbook p=.42, LSAT p=.68). Adaptive explanation also not better (Beer p=.31).
limits: Adaptive explanations were a designed fix; it failed in this test.
agent_relevance: A model's own fluent rationale persuades its reader (including a second model pass). Do not use rationale as a verifier.

source: Bansal et al. (2021) review of prior work, Table 1
finding: In prior explanation studies, the AI alone beat the best human-AI team every time.
numbers: Deception-detection: human 51.1%, AI 87.0%, team 74.6% (another: 54.6/86.3/74.0). Income: 65/75/73. Nutrition: 0.46/0.75/0.74.
limits: Selected examples chosen by the authors for closest human/AI match.
agent_relevance: Typical published gains from adding people to strong models are catch-up, not synergy.

source: Bucinca, Malaya, Gajos (2021) To trust or to think: cognitive forcing functions
finding: Forcing a person to think first (update, wait, on-demand) cut overreliance versus plain explanations, but did not raise total accuracy.
numbers: N=199 analysed per abstract (260 recruited, 49 filtered). Simulated AI 75% accurate. On AI-wrong items, forcing functions gave more correct choices (chi2(2,N=663)=13.30, p=.0013); overall performance no difference between forcing and plain XAI.
limits: Single task (swap carb ingredient); team still worse than the AI alone; users trusted and liked forced designs least.
agent_relevance: Delayed or order-controlled review (decide first, then see the other opinion) is a tested design lever. It costs acceptability.

source: Bucinca, Malaya, Gajos (2021) To trust or to think: cognitive forcing functions
finding: Benefit of forcing depended on need for cognition.
numbers: High-NFC participants overall performance 0.44 vs low-NFC 0.23 (F(1,172.5)=29.13). Forcing helped high-NFC on AI-wrong items (chi2=13.12, p=.001, N=357) but not low-NFC overall (chi2=2.01, N=306).
limits: Median split; post hoc subgroup.
agent_relevance: Interventions that demand effort help only those who engage; prompts that ask a model for effort may likewise be skipped.

source: Vasconcelos et al. (2023) Explanations can reduce overreliance on AI systems during decision-making
finding: Overreliance is a cost-benefit choice: explanations reduce it only when checking them is cheaper than doing the task.
numbers: Five studies, N=731 total (340, 340, 286, 114, 76). Easy maze: AI and XAI overreliance equal. Harder mazes: XAI overreliance lower. Higher pay for accuracy cut overreliance (Study 4).
limits: Maze task with simulated AI; cost scale is made-up units; money effects from crowd workers.
agent_relevance: Verification step must be cheaper than regeneration. Design checks as short, mechanical verifications.

source: Vasconcelos et al. (2023), Study 5 (Cognitive Effort Discounting)
finding: People assign more value to easier-to-read explanations and to explanations on harder tasks.
numbers: Study 5 N=76: utility higher for easy-to-understand explanations and for harder tasks, matching the framework.
limits: Small N; lab proxy for utility.
agent_relevance: Rival account to Bucinca's dual-process account; explains the earlier null on explanations.

source: Kim et al. (2024) I'm not sure, but: LLM uncertainty expression and user reliance
finding: Access to a (fictional) LLM answer lowered accuracy overall; first-person hedges raised it.
numbers: Pre-registered, N=404, medical questions. Accuracy Control (AI, no hedge) 63.9% vs No-AI 74.2%. With AI correct: 88.5% vs 77.9%. With AI incorrect: 33.0% vs 64.7%.
limits: Fictional search engine; fixed share of wrong answers; short questions.
agent_relevance: Plain LLM output pulls a reader to its errors (about 32 points lost when wrong). Hedging text can lower the pull.

source: Kim et al. (2024) I'm not sure, but: LLM uncertainty expression and user reliance
finding: Uncertainty phrased in first person (I'm not sure) cut agreement and raised accuracy; general-perspective phrasing was weaker, not significant.
numbers: First-person lowered confidence and agreement and raised accuracy; exploratory analysis: gain comes from less overreliance on wrong answers, not eliminated.
limits: Exploratory mediation; one domain; static text.
agent_relevance: Wording of a model's self-report matters to the joint system. A program can map internal confidence to first-person hedge text.

source: Peng, Kalliamvakou, Cihon, Demirer (2023) Impact of AI on developer productivity: GitHub Copilot
finding: Randomized trial, simple task: Copilot group finished 55.8% faster.
numbers: N=95 (45 treated, 50 control), write an HTTP server in JavaScript. Mean time 71.17 vs 160.89 min, p=0.0017, 95% CI 21-89%. Gains larger for less experienced and older developers.
limits: Known-pattern synthetic task, likely in training data; four control outliers over 300 min; participants mostly India/Pakistan, low income.
agent_relevance: Gain is large on well-trodden tasks. Do not carry the number to novel work.

source: Becker, Rush, Barnes, Rein (METR, 2025) Early-2025 AI and experienced open-source developer productivity
finding: RCT in real repositories: allowing AI made experienced developers 19% slower.
numbers: 16 developers, 246 issues (136 AI-allowed, 110 not), mean 2.0 h, repos averaging 23,000 stars. Cursor Pro with Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet. Slowdown 19%.
limits: Small N of developers; 2025 tools; high-familiarity mature codebases; authors do not claim it generalizes.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that benchmark gains do not carry to experts on familiar hard work. Measure real end-to-end time.

source: Becker, Rush, Barnes, Rein (METR, 2025) Early-2025 AI and experienced open-source developer productivity
finding: Both developers and experts mis-predicted direction of effect.
numbers: Developers forecast -24% time before, estimated -20% after. 34 economists forecast -39%, 54 ML experts -38%. Actual +19%.
limits: Forecasts were self-report; selection into study possible.
agent_relevance: Perceived help from a tool is a poor guide to actual joint performance. Use measured outcomes.

source: Becker, Rush, Barnes, Rein (METR, 2025) Early-2025 AI and experienced open-source developer productivity
finding: Where the time went; which causes were checked.
numbers: Screen labels (143 h of video): less time coding and reading; more time prompting, waiting, reviewing AI output, idle. About 9% of time reviewing/cleaning AI output (44 valid recordings). 21 candidate factors: 5 supported, 10 mixed, 6 against. No difference by prior Cursor experience in first 50 h.
limits: Not powered for subgroup tests; authors caution against individual factors.
agent_relevance: Review and wait overhead is the cost line of a joint system. Count it.

source: Becker, Rush, Barnes, Rein (METR, 2025) Early-2025 AI and experienced open-source developer productivity
finding: Slowdown larger on tasks where developers had high prior exposure and low need for outside resources.
numbers: Moderate evidence from self-rated task exposure (1-5 scale) and external resource need.
limits: Self-rated, moderate evidence only.
agent_relevance: Tool help shrinks where the human already holds the context; gains are largest where the human lacks knowledge.

source: Brynjolfsson, Li, Raymond (2023) Generative AI at work
finding: Field rollout to 5,179 support agents: +14% chats resolved per hour; +34% for novices; little for experts.
numbers: Staggered deployment, N=5,179 agents. Workers followed the AI suggestion 35% of the time on average; returns higher for those who followed. Newer agents moved down the experience curve faster.
limits: Single firm, one tool, chat support; working paper revised Nov 2023; attrition result lacks agent fixed effects.
agent_relevance: Tool-as-teacher effect: skill gap shrinks. The human chose when to follow, about 1 in 3.

source: Dell'Acqua et al. (2023/2026) Navigating the jagged technological frontier
finding: Preregistered field experiment with 758 BCG consultants: big gains inside the AI frontier, loss outside it.
numbers: Inside, 18 tasks: +12.2% tasks completed (control 82%, GPT 91%, GPT+overview 93%), 25.1% faster, quality up. Outside (one business task): correct 84.5% control vs 60% and 70.6% with AI, about 19 percentage points lower.
limits: Outside-frontier arm is one task; prompt-training arm did worse there (24.5% vs 13.9% drop); PDF read from a mirror copy; journal version Organization Science 2026.
agent_relevance: Capability is jagged and users cannot see the edge. The program should keep a task-type map of where model help is safe.

source: Dell'Acqua et al. (2023/2026), skill moderation
finding: Bottom-half skill subjects gained most, in line with Noy and Zhang.
numbers: Both skill halves improved inside the frontier; bottom half gained more (paper Fig. 4; exact per-half numbers not recorded here).
limits: Exact numbers not recorded.
agent_relevance: Same compression as in customer-support data: model help equalises.

source: Lee et al. (2025) Impact of generative AI on critical thinking (survey of knowledge workers)
finding: Higher confidence in the AI went with less self-reported critical thinking; higher self-confidence with more.
numbers: N=319 workers, 936 examples (39.96% creation, 32.37% information, 27.67% advice). Critical thinking enacted in 555 examples (59.29%).
limits: Self-report survey; correlational; no performance measure.
agent_relevance: Trust in the partner drives how much checking the human does. In an agent, high trust in its own draft means skipped checks.

source: Kosmyna et al. (2025) Your brain on ChatGPT
finding: EEG study: LLM-essay writers showed different, weaker-engagement neural patterns; Brain-to-LLM switchers showed higher connectivity.
numbers: 54 participants in sessions 1-3 (18 per group: LLM, search, brain-only); 18 completed session 4 (LLM-to-Brain, Brain-to-LLM). Brain-to-LLM connectivity higher than LLM group sessions 1-3.
limits: Preprint, not peer-reviewed at read time; small N; essay task; EEG over-interpretation risk.
agent_relevance: Weak, preliminary. Offloading too early may reduce the human's own model of the task.

source: Bainbridge (1983) Ironies of automation
finding: Automating the routine leaves people the hard exceptions with less practice and little feedback.
numbers: No numbers; conceptual paper.
limits: Not opened this session; stated from prior knowledge.
agent_relevance: Foundation for why joint systems fail on edge cases.

source: Parasuraman and Manzey (2010) Complacency and bias in human use of automation
finding: Complacency and automation bias occur in experts and novices, are not removed by training alone, and rise under multitask load.
numbers: No numbers recorded.
limits: Not opened this session; stated from prior knowledge.
agent_relevance: Same failure appears in people and in LLM agents trusting tool output.

source: Hollnagel and Woods (2005) Joint Cognitive Systems: Foundations of Cognitive Systems Engineering
finding: Define the system by what it does (control and coping) rather than by its parts; describe the joint system, not human and machine separately.
numbers: No numbers.
limits: Book not opened; framing only.
agent_relevance: Basis for treating program plus model as one unit measured on joint outcomes.
